chapter: The Lunceford years: Europe, rivals and bandsmen
title: Underpaid Sy Oliver and the Lunceford-Oxley ownership
summary: Crawford says Sy resented his low pay and that Lunceford turned out to be a hired man whose road manager Dutch Williams handed him money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, how did he -- being as good a musician as he was, being paid as poorly as he was being paid, but Lunceford, how did he react to that?
Well, he still wanted to go out there

and throw some dirt on Lunceford's grave in his face. Due to the fact that he knew he was getting so underpaid, he was being underpaid so badly. You couldn't change Lunceford's, Oxley's mind. Oh, man, don't let me get started talking about him myself. Because -- is this on?

Because after all the time that I spent in that band, I used to see Dutch Williams, who was the road manager -- getting a little tired now, but I'm going to finish this. Come by every night after the job in the bus, and would give Lunceford some money.

Well, later on -- Mose Allen discovered it, bass player -- that Lunceford was a hired man, just like we were in the band. Now, Lunceford's dead, Oxley's dead, but I can say it, and I'm saying it. He was hired just like we were. And yet, Lunceford was the owner and the leader of the band. Only he was getting very paid every night and we got paid every week.
Was this before or after Irving Mills got involved with this band?
Do you think Irving Mills was involved in the band being taken over like that?
Well, I don't know, but you bet your life Oxley got his training from somebody, because

Lunceford was getting -- I don't know how much he was getting, but Dutch Williams would come by every night in that bus after we finished a gig, on his way up to the front of the bus to talk with the driver, but he'd always stop at Lunceford's seat which was the second or the first seat.
